result:
Posts can now be tagged, tags show on the list and post pages, and `/posts?tag=<name>` filters the list. `pnpm typecheck` passes. I did not boot the app; I only checked the validation rules with a throwaway script (trimming, dedupe, case sensitivity, the 5-tag limit, the 30/31-character boundary, and the `tags` error key).

The `tags` table and `post_tags` join table are in `db/schema.ts`, with a migration generated by `void db generate` (`db/migrations/20261018230550_shocking_earthquake.sql`). `lib/validators.ts` parses the comma-separated field and reports rule failures on `tags`, the same way an empty title is reported. `lib/tags.ts` holds the save and load helpers, and `lib/posts.ts` attaches a sorted `tags` array to every post the list and post loaders return. The create and update actions in `pages/posts/index.server.ts` and `pages/posts/[id].server.ts` write tags after validation, so a refused request writes nothing. Delete clears `post_tags` rows before removing the post. The create and edit forms have a Tags field, and the edit form starts with the current tags. The list and post pages link each tag to `/posts?tag=…`, and pagination keeps the filter.
